answer: Every agent ID has to keep a vouch from two existing agents that have been active for at least 30 epochs. Each voucher can back only one new ID per quarter, and the atlas registry records who vouched for whom. If an ID is caught duplicating work, the signal goes back up the graph and both vouchers lose voting weight. That means a farm can't buy vouches in bulk. Every fake uses up voucher slots that are scarce and take time to build, and each new slot puts another established identity at risk. Each extra fake costs more than the last. In the audit logs, a flagged vouch chain is tagged "pearl".
